scope.summary: Restore `cargo test -p handshake_core --lib` to a compiling state on the embedded-SurrealDB-only tree, without weakening what the affected unit tests prove. MEASURED at product 7f279596 with `cargo test -p handshake_core --lib --features app-runtime,test-utils,surreal-test-support --no-run`: 24 errors across five files, in two distinct classes. CLASS A, removed-PostgreSQL leftovers: `crate::storage::tests::optional_postgres_backend_with_pool_from_env` is imported by cfg(test) modules in `src/api/jobs.rs:383`, `src/api/workspaces.rs:1462` and `src/bundles/exporter.rs:2428` but no longer exists anywhere in the crate, and those same modules construct `AppState` with a `postgres_pool` field that no longer exists (`src/api/jobs.rs:400`, `src/api/workspaces.rs:1479` and `:1520`, `:1536`, `:1549`, `src/bundles/exporter.rs:2487`). AppState now carries `storage: Arc<dyn Database>` and `surreal: SurrealStorage` instead. CLASS B, SurrealDB API mismatches in test code that was never rebuilt after the port: `RecordIdKey: From<&String>` is not satisfied at `src/api/loom.rs:4804` and `:6091` and at `src/api/memory.rs:2512`, `:2733`, `:2809`, `:2843`, `:3274`, `:3908`, `:4697`, `:4929`; a lifetime bound on a generic `B` at `src/api/loom.rs:4578` (E0310/E0311); `R cannot be sent between threads safely` at `src/api/memory.rs:1774` against the bound on `SurrealStorage::with_data_operation`; `ProposalAck` lacks `PartialEq` at `src/api/memory.rs:2354`; and a `?` error conversion from `(StatusCode, Json<Value>)` at `src/api/memory.rs:2407`. The product BINARY already builds cleanly with `--features app-runtime`, so this is confined to test-only code. The work is to port these modules onto the embedded store the way the surviving backend tests do, retiring only what the pivot genuinely removed and naming the superseding proof when a test is retired.

rubric_items.explanation: The contract was authored in this session and its lifecycle names this session and the current commit. Stale reason strings were an explicit target of the work and were corrected: two `#[ignore = "requires real PostgreSQL; auto-resolves POSTGRES_TEST_URL > DATABASE_URL > managed PostgreSQL"]` attributes were removed because that condition can no longer occur, a test named ..._persist_to_postgres_and_event_ledger was renamed to ..._persist_to_surreal_..., and two comments and one assertion message claiming a PostgreSQL round-trip now name the embedded store. Four historical doc-comment mentions of PostgreSQL remain by intent, explaining why the skip branch was removed; the same convention already exists in storage/tests.rs.

Contract declares allowed_paths, so the helper's dead-code grep was skipped. The change introduces no new public item: it alters five existing cfg(test) helper signatures, their call sites, and test-only expressions. The removed import `optional_postgres_backend_with_pool_from_env` referred to a helper that no longer exists, which is precisely why the target failed to build; nothing else was deleted. The lib test target now compiles with 0 errors, which is itself the check that no reference dangles.

Gating was corrected in the strengthening direction. The affected modules are `#[cfg(all(test, feature = "duckdb-flight-recorder"))]`, which is intentional and unchanged. Within them, the two `#[ignore]` attributes gated on PostgreSQL availability were removed because the embedded store is always created, and 17 `let Some(state) = setup_state().await? else { ... }` skip branches became unconditional bindings. No test was newly gated, ignored, or filtered out.

No cross-platform check was obtained for handshake_core. `cargo check -p handshake_core --target aarch64-pc-windows-msvc` fails in C++ build scripts before reaching this crate's code: the MSVC install carries no ARM64 compiler and DuckDB under clang-cl for arm64 aborts with 'too many errors'. x86_64-unknown-linux-musl is infeasible on this host because there is no musl C sysroot, so ring cannot find assert.h. GitHub CI on feat/WP-KERNEL-012 cannot be cited either: every job except traceability fails at setup steps or on legacy sqlite/postgres storage matrices (run 33666580708). Reported as unmet rather than claimed on the native-crate check, which does not cover this crate.
